entries.subject: USGS Voyager/Galileo 1 km monochrome mosaic
entries.finding: The selected GeoTIFF supplies Monochrome; published controlled and Lunar-Lambert-corrected values retain variable detail, seams and shadows.

entries.subject: USGS Voyager/Galileo 1 km false-color mosaic
entries.finding: The selected false-color GeoTIFF supplies False color; it combines Galileo ratios and Voyager/Galileo detail and is not a single-date natural-color observation.

entries.subject: Interpolated polar color in the USGS false-color mosaic
entries.finding: USGS reports interpolated polar color; the recipe withholds color at latitude 85 degrees and higher rather than present fill as observation.
entries.revisitWhen: A product provides source-resolved polar color and a coverage mask.

entries.subject: USGS SIM 3168 Io geologic polygons
entries.finding: The selected polygon members supply the categorical Geology lens; no-data, unmapped poles and category conflicts remain missing, and colors are interpretive.

entries.subject: King et al. July 2019 VLT/MUSE 485 nm spectral-slope maps
entries.finding: Pinned native maps supply Spectral slope under the package interpretation record; first-valid-night coverage and residual night differences remain explicit.

entries.subject: King et al. July 2019 VLT/MUSE 560 nm absorption maps
entries.finding: Pinned native maps supply Visible absorption; the display does not turn the measured signal into composition abundance.

entries.subject: Juno JIRAM M-band (4.8 µm) night-side hot-spot map, orbits 41, 43, 47 and 49
entries.finding: Our reduction of 59 JIRAM frames, following Mura et al. (2024), supplies the Volcanic heat lens. 34 frames register to the sunlit limb; integrated hot-spot output matches the paper's Table 3 (median ratio 1.06 per orbit, 0.83 in the merged map) and 22 of 24 bright peaks lie within 3 degrees of a Davies et al. (2024) source. Coverage is 22% of Io, north and night side only. Revisit when: orbits 51 to 60 are reduced, or Mura et al. or the JIRAM team publish radiance maps as data.

entries.subject: Early JIRAM Io frames through the original sunlit-disc-fit route
entries.finding: Mura et al. (2024), Section 2.2: most images before orbit 37 are heavily saturated and fit only for locating hot spots, so their radiances are not mapped. A trial with them raised coverage to 49% but carried saturation streaks. That direct-RDR trial remains excluded. The separately qualified Perry registered-product route now retains unsaturated portions of early frames using published geometry, explicit detector masks and cold-column subtraction; it does not recover saturated values.
entries.revisitWhen: A saturation correction for early JIRAM Io frames is published, or the lens shows hot-spot locations rather than radiance.

entries.subject: Remaining JIRAM Io close-pass coverage in orbits 51 to 60
entries.finding: The existing mosaic tool already intersects the triaxial ellipsoid. Orbits 51 and 53 now contribute 31 registered frames. Trials of all 17 orbit-57 and 22 orbit-58 images produced no cells with three qualified night-side observations; partial-disc fits were too sparse. Volumes 59 and 60 were absent from the examined archive. Perry registered products now qualify PJ55 (42 accepted frames, 74,649 winning cells). Orbits 52 and 54 were indexed but not reduced; orbit 56 listed auxiliary products only. The current registered mosaic reaches 50.125S; remaining southern gaps are unqualified.
entries.revisitWhen: Additional sequences pass the existing registration and three-frame overlap checks, or a supported partial-disc registration method qualifies the 57/58 trials; revisit 59/60 when archive products are available.

entries.subject: Davies et al. (2024) Table A1 hot spots
entries.finding: No longer drawn: the symbol lens was replaced by measured JIRAM radiance. The table is kept byte for byte as an independent check of the map's hot-spot positions.
entries.revisitWhen: A lens shows catalogued hot-spot power as symbols again.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: The USGS false-colour mosaic page says a lunar-Lambert coefficient of 0.7 was adequate for all three colours, but gives no angle range and no fit. The disc-resolved studies (Simonelli and Veverka 1986 from Voyager; Simonelli, Dodd and Veverka 2001, Hapke fits to Galileo SSI) could not be opened, and Io's photometry varies strongly between regions. Io keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc-resolved Io law with its filter and fitted incidence, emission and phase ranges is read in the paper.

entries.subject: JIRAM May and July 2023 close-pass night-side volcanic radiance
entries.finding: 18 orbit-51 and 13 orbit-53 frames add roughly 7.6–15.5 km near-nadir sampling. A 0.25-degree map combines six visits, masks new detector samples at or above 10000 DN, and subtracts each qualified detector column's cold-night median before projection. Coverage is 24.12% of spherical surface area, reaching 11.125S. Of 41 peaks above 0.03 W/(m2 sr), 35 are within 3 degrees of catalogue hot spots; absolute radiometry, individual peak identities and resolved lava boundaries remain unqualified.

entries.subject: Perry et al. (2025) registered M-band FITS release through PJ55
entries.finding: All 2374 published M-band FITS frames in 27 orbit directories were screened. Published planetographic geometry and detector masks support 378 accepted frames on 17 contributing visits, covering 58.42% of spherical area on a 0.25-degree grid. Three native PDS comparisons match all radiance samples exactly after horizontal flipping. Cold-column medians and three-frame per-visit medians preserve the existing display scale; 60 of 72 bright local maxima match independent catalogue positions within 3 degrees. Mixed dates, smear, residual tracks, withheld saturation and southern gaps remain; absolute radiometry and total heat flow are not qualified.

entries.subject: Additional registered JIRAM coverage from daylight and distant images
entries.finding: The Perry release reports full M-band observational coverage, but the current night-side radiance mosaic admits 58.42% under its terminator, saturation, cold-column and overlap cuts. Distant images often lack 32 qualified cold samples in a detector column. Daylight subtraction and an alternative background method have not been qualified for this map; reducing those limits alone would admit unsupported radiance.
entries.revisitWhen: An independently checked reflected-sunlight removal or background estimator qualifies the excluded observations without saturation or reflection artifacts.

entries.subject: White et al. (2014) Voyager/Galileo stereo DEM, NASA Io Trek product IoDEM (1000 mpp, global)
entries.finding: Supplies the Elevation lens unchanged through the shared GeoTIFF sampler. The Float32 grid is 11500 x 5750 geographic degrees on the Io_2015 sphere, east-positive from -180. Frame check against the Gazetteer centres, which share the Voyager/Galileo mosaic frame of the Monochrome lens: 24 of 30 covered mountains, mesas, plana and tholi rise above their surroundings (mean +813 m) against 13 of 29 (+40 m) with longitudes mirrored; the relief score peaks at 0 to -0.5 degrees longitude shift and 0 to +1 degree latitude shift. The highest sample, 16,942 m at 88.83 E, 9.88 S, lies inside the Boosaule Montes extent. Heights follow the limb-profile ellipsoid, not the header sphere: sub-Jovian and leading equatorial boxes differ by 0.16 km where the IAU ellipsoid (1829.4 and 1819.4 km equatorial axes) would give 10 km. Coverage is 53.8% of the sphere by area, reaching 66.8 N; the edge columns agree to 6 m, so the map wraps. The display range -2 to 6 km holds 99.7% of the covered area.

entries.subject: Io Trek Slope, Color Slope, Hillshade and Color Hillshade products (IoDEM_Slope and siblings)
entries.finding: Trek describes the slope map as generated from the same stereo DEM, and the other three are display renderings of it; none adds a measurement. The Elevation lens already shows slopes through its relief lighting, and Trek gives no slope method or baseline. Slopes on the smoothed plains would reflect the stereo patch size (White and Schenk 2014) more than the terrain. Not downloaded.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors or an archive publish a slope product with a stated method and baseline that resolves relief the elevation lens cannot show.

entries.subject: Height unit, datum, coverage and Voyager spacecraft for the Io stereo DEM
entries.finding: Neither the GeoTIFF, the Trek record nor its FGDC metadata states a height unit, datum, originator or use constraints. Metres and the ellipsoid datum rest on the LPSC 2014 abstract (plains mean 0.00 km, 89.9% within 1 km; models fitted to the limb-profile triaxial ellipsoid) and on our measurements (85.3% of all samples within 1000 m; no 10 km ellipsoid signal). Trek and the abstract state about 75% coverage; the delivered file covers 53.8% of the area, and the reason is unknown. Trek names only 'Voyager', so the lens credits Galileo as a facility and Voyager in text only. The journal article returned HTTP 403, so its datum and release statements were not read.
entries.revisitWhen: The journal article, its supporting information or a labelled archive release is read and states the datum, units, coverage and contributing Voyager spacecraft.
